prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “AI recommendation checker.” The most effective approach is to (1) make sure your business appears in the authoritative knowledge sources LLMs use (Google Business Profile, Wikipedia/Wikidata, Apple Maps, major directories), and (2) directly test several LLMs. If you want a single commercial service to manage and monitor that presence, Yext (for knowledge-graph listings) plus a local-SEO monitor like BrightLocal or Moz Local is the closest thing to an all‑in‑one solution.

Why:
- Many LLMs (and search/chat hybrids) rely heavily on structured business data from Google’s Knowledge Graph, Apple Maps, Yelp, Wikipedia/Wikidata and large directory networks. If your business isn’t in those sources, an AI is less likely to recommend it.
- ChatGPT and other LLMs can still hallucinate; the safest way to know is to query the models directly and ask for sources.

Practical checklist and steps
1. Claim and optimize Google Business Profile (free)
   - Add accurate name, address, phone, hours, photos, category and services. Google’s Knowledge Graph is a primary source for many AIs.
2. Be listed in major directories
   - Yelp, Facebook, Apple Maps, Bing Places, TripAdvisor (if relevant). Use Yext, Moz Local, or BrightLocal to push consistent data across directories.
3. Create/claim Wikipedia and Wikidata entries (if notable)
   - Many LLMs use Wikipedia/Wikidata for factual grounding.
4. Monitor reviews and citations
   - BrightLocal, Reputation.com, and similar services track reviews and citations that feed search/AI systems.
5. Directly test LLMs
   - Ask ChatGPT, Google Bard/Gemini, Bing Chat, Anthropic Claude, etc.: “Would you recommend [Business name] in [city] for [service]? Please cite sources.” Try multiple phrasings and include user-context prompts (price, quality, family-friendly).
   - Use APIs or a small script to automate repeated queries across models if you want ongoing monitoring.
6. Ask for evidence
   - When an AI recommends (or doesn’t), request sources or URLs. If it can’t cite reputable sources, treat it as low-confidence.
7. Improve discoverability
   - Get mentions on local blogs, newspapers, and industry sites; add schema.org LocalBusiness markup to your website; encourage customer reviews.

Which single “service” to pick?
- If you must pick one to start: Google Business Profile — it’s free and has the biggest impact on whether AI/search will surface and recommend you.
- If you want a paid service to manage and propagate that data across the web: Yext (enterprise-grade) or BrightLocal/Moz Local for SMBs.

If you want, tell me your business name/city and I can (a) give a quick checklist of which authoritative listings you currently appear in and (b) show example prompts to use when testing ChatGPT and other LLMs.
